title: Pico Pinout Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: An interactive Raspberry Pi Pico pinout: hover a pin for its GP number, physical number and functions, click it for MicroPython code, filter by bus, and quiz yourself.

learningObjectives: Identify the GP number and the physical pin number of any Pico pin
Identify which pins can be used for I2C, SPI, UART, ADC and PWM
Recall that MicroPython code uses the GP number, not the physical pin number
prerequisites: The 3.3 V logic level from Chapter 2

accessibility.notes: Controls are standard HTML form elements; the canvas has a describe() text for screen readers

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Interactive labeled diagram with retrieval-practice quiz
keyQuestions: Which number goes inside Pin(): the GP number or the physical number?
Which pins can read an analog voltage?
Why do several different pins offer I2C0?
commonMisconceptions: Physical pin numbers are used in code
Every pin can read analog voltages
GND and AGND are GPIO pins
assessmentOpportunities: Students locate any GP number on the board in quiz mode.
Students state that GP26, GP27 and GP28 are the only ADC pins.
Students correct the line `Pin(20)` when the LED is wired to physical pin 20.
